title: Synthesizing scientific literature with retrieval-augmented language models
impact: OpenScholar combines a 45-million-paper store, bi-encoder retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, iterative self-feedback and citation verification; it is the strongest peer-reviewed blueprint found for long-form scientific synthesis.

title: Evaluating and Guarding Citation Faithfulness in Agentic Scientific Synthesis
impact: Shows citation-verifier conclusions vary materially with verifier strictness; proposes gold-anchored calibration and split-conformal bounds for unsupported citations.

title: Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine: A Large-Scale, Systematic Expert Evaluation and Practical Insights
impact: 18 medical experts and 80,502 annotations show naive RAG can degrade medical answers; evidence filtering and query reformulation are high-value interventions.

title: HydraRAG: Structured Cross-Source Enhanced Large Language Model Reasoning
impact: Combines graph topology, document semantics and source reliability with cross-source corroboration and entity-path alignment for multi-hop verification.

title: Medical Graph RAG: Evidence-based Medical Large Language Model via Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
impact: Medical GraphRAG architecture links private user documents to credible medical sources and balances top-down precise retrieval with bottom-up refinement.

title: Rationale-Guided Retrieval Augmented Generation for Medical Question Answering
impact: RAG-squared uses rationale-guided query reformulation, distractor filtering and balanced retrieval across four biomedical corpora.

title: Uncertainty-aware large language models for explainable disease diagnosis
impact: ConfiDx aligns models to diagnostic criteria and explicitly identifies and explains missing-evidence uncertainty; supports criterion-level abstention.

title: Large Language Models lack essential metacognition for reliable medical reasoning
impact: MetaMedQA shows strong medical-answer accuracy does not imply reliable self-assessment; models remain overconfident on unanswerable or malformed questions.

title: Large language model agents can use tools to perform clinical calculations
impact: Task-specific deterministic clinical calculators sharply reduce calculation errors compared with unaided generation, RAG or generic code execution.

title: Evaluating base and retrieval augmented LLMs with document or online support for evidence based neurology
impact: Guideline-grounded document RAG improved correctness and citations, but case-based questions remained harder and harmful answers were not eliminated.

title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Can be More Effective than Scaling Parameters for Reasoning
impact: Adaptive allocation of inference compute and process-verifier-guided search can outperform uniform best-of-N, especially when matched to task difficulty.

title: Language agents achieve superhuman synthesis of scientific knowledge
impact: PaperQA2 provides an agentic blueprint for full-text literature search, cited synthesis and contradiction detection with expert evaluation.

title: RAGChecker: A Fine-grained Framework for Diagnosing Retrieval-Augmented Generation
impact: Claim-level entailment diagnostics separate retrieval failures from generation failures and correlate better with human judgement than coarse scores.

title: ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
impact: Evaluates context relevance, answer faithfulness and answer relevance using lightweight judges calibrated with a small human-labelled set.

title: Model Internals-based Answer Attribution for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
impact: MIRAGE attributes context-sensitive answer tokens to contributing documents using model-internal saliency rather than trusting self-generated citations alone.

title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models
impact: Draft, plan independent verification questions, answer them without draft anchoring, then regenerate a verified response.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
impact: Learns retrieval-on-demand and explicit relevance, support and utility reflection signals, improving factuality and citation accuracy.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
impact: Retrieval quality gating, fallback search and decompose-then-recompose filtering improve robustness when first-pass retrieval is poor.

title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
impact: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback is unreliable and can degrade reasoning, supporting independent verifier and tool-based checks.

title: Let's Verify Step by Step
impact: Process supervision and step-level reward models outperform outcome-only supervision in the reported math setting and motivate step-verifier architectures.
